references.text: Gideon had previously asked the men of Sukkot for bread for his exhausted troops, but they mocked him and refused to help. Now he returns with the captured kings as proof of his victory.
The men of Sukkot mocked Gideon by asking if he had already captured Zebah and Zalmunna. This is the scornful remark Gideon now refers to.
Gideon captured Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings, and put their entire army to flight. This is the fulfillment of the victory he now displays.
After confronting the men of Sukkot with the captured kings, Gideon carries out the punishment he had promised them for their mockery and refusal to help.
Sukkot is first mentioned as a place where Jacob settled and built shelters for his livestock, which gave the place its name.
